topic.name: The Shell Method: Rotation About the Y-Axis

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=x^2-x^3$ and the $x$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} x^2-x^3 & = 0 \\[5pt] x^2(1-x) & =0 \end{align*} The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x\, f(x) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1} x\left( x^2-x^3 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1} \left( x^3-x^4 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \left. 2\pi \left(\dfrac{x^4}{4}\ - \dfrac{x^5}{5} \right)\right|_{0}^{1}\\[5pt] &= 2\pi \left[ \left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)-0 \right] \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \left( \dfrac{1}{20} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{10} \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=3x^2-x^3$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3x^2-x^3 &= 0 \\[5pt] x^2(3-x) &= 0 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=3.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x\, f(x) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{3} x \left( 3x^2-x^3 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{3} \left( 3x^3-x^4 \right) \textrm{d}x \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Volume of a Solid Using the Shell Method

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $y=4x-2x^2$ and $y=2x^3,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
First, let $f(x)=4x-2x^2$ and $g(x)=2x^3.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f(x) &=g(x) \\[5pt] 4x-2x^2 &= 2x^3 \\[5pt] 4x-2x^2-2x^3 &= 0 \\[5pt] -2x(-2+x+x^2) &= 0 \\[5pt] x(x-1)(x+2)&=0\\ \end{align*}

The solutions are $x=-2, $ $x=0,$ and $x=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=1$ because we are only concerned about $x \geq 0.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=2x^3,$ and

  • leaves through the upper function $y=f(x)=4x-2x^2.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x \big( \big[ {\color{brown}\text{upper}} \big] - \big[ {\color{blue}\text{lower}} \big] \big) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1} x \left( [{\color{brown}4x-2x^2}] - [{\color{blue}2x^3}] \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1} x\left(4x-2x^2-2x^3 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 4\pi \int_{0}^{1} \left( 2x^2-x^3 -x^4\right) \textrm{d}x \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Volume of a Solid When a Region is Enclosed Between Two Curves

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $y=-x^2+2x+1$ and $y=x^2+1,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
First, let $f(x)=-x^2+2x+1$ and $g(x)=x^2+1.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f(x) &= g(x) \\[5pt] -x^2+2x+1 &=x^2+1 \\[5pt] -2x^2+2x &= 0 \\[5pt] -2x(x-1) &= 0 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

The solutions are $x=0,$ and $x=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=x^2+1,$ and

  • leaves through the upper function $y=f(x)=-x^2+2x+1.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x \big( \big[ {\color{brown}\text{upper}} \big] - \big[ {\color{blue}\text{lower}} \big] \big) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1} x \left( [{\color{brown}-x^2+2x+1}] - [{\color{blue}x^2+1}] \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1} x \left( 2x-2x^2 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 4\pi \int_{0}^{1} \left( x^2-x^3\right) \textrm{d}x \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Volume of a Solid When a Region is Enclosed Between Two Curves

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=x-3x^2$ and the $x$-axis. Calculate the volume $V$ of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $y$-axis. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} x-3x^2 &= 0 \\[5pt] x(1-3x) &= 0 \end{align*}

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=\dfrac{1}{3}.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=\dfrac{1}{3}.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} x\, f(x) \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1/3} x\left( x-3x^2 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1/3} \left( x^2-3x^3 \right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \left. \left( \dfrac{x^3}{3} - \dfrac{3x^4}{4} \right) \right|_{0}^{1/3} \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \left[ \left(\dfrac{1}{3\cdot 3^3} - \dfrac {3}{4\cdot 3^4} \right) -0 \right]\\[5pt] &= 2\pi \left( \dfrac{1}{324} \right) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{\pi}{162}} \end{align*}
